Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please press star one if you have a question, and instructions will follow. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a standout performance in Q3, underscoring our leadership in the Aerospace & Defense sector against a backdrop of sustained geopolitical tensions, robust DoD budgets, and accelerating commercial recovery. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Let me highlight our overall company performance highlights and key takeaways.

Q3 revenue came in at $24.5 billion, up 13% year-over-year and 7% organically, surpassing our guidance midpoint by $350 million. This extends our streak of eight straight quarters of double-digit growth, powered by a balanced mix across Defense Systems at 48% of revenue, Commercial Aviation at 42%, and Space & Advanced Technologies plus Services at 10%. Adjusted EPS reached $3.15, up 17% from last year, thanks to operating leverage and tight cost controls. Free cash flow hit $2.6 billion, a 22% YoY increase, strengthening our balance sheet to a net debt to EBITDA of 1.1x.

Funded backlog hit a record $92 billion, up 10% from Q2, offering over 5 years of revenue visibility at current rates. Book-to-bill stood at 1.25x, boosted by marquee awards like a $3.8 billion IDIQ for F-35 sustainment and upgrades, plus $2.5 billion from the U.S. Space Force for proliferated satellite constellations under PWSA.

In Defense Systems, we posted $11.8 billion in revenue, up 8% YoY, with EBIT margins up 110 basis points to 14.5%. Hypersonics and missile defense led, as our boost-glide vehicle program entered low-rate production, grabbing significant share amid Indo-Pacific tensions. International sales rose 20%, highlighted by a $1.0 billion PAC-3 MSE order from Poland leveraging NATO aid.

Commercial Aviation surged to $10.3 billion, up 25% YoY, with widebody output aligning at 90% of contracted rates for 787 and 777X equivalents, deliveries climbing 28% to 42 units. Supply chains stabilized, titanium costs down 12% via allied sourcing. Asia-Pacific demand doubled quarter-over-quarter on fleet expansions, despite European engine delays boosting our MRO.

Space & Advanced Technologies delivered $2.4 billion, up 10% YoY at 13.2% margins. First flights on Vulcan upper stage variants supported ULA's NSSL launches, while our Valkyrie drone hit 450 test hours for CCA programs.

Cash enabled $1.1 billion in repurchases and a 9% dividend increase to $0.82 per share. R&D up 11% to $1.0 billion, emphasizing digital twins and AI maintenance cutting F-35 times by 18%. Emissions dropped 16% YoY with SAF integration.

Regionally, U.S. DoD was 62% of bookings, EMEA up 18% on F-35 exports, Middle East +32% from Iron Dome work. Labor gaps filled with 4,500 AI hires.

Strategically, 68% fixed-price revenue shields us, tuck-ins like RF seeker buys add radar tech. Q4 guide: $25.0-25.6 billion revenue, FY24 EPS $12.40-12.80.

This validates our fortress balance sheet and innovation focus in an $850 billion market growing 5% CAGR. John, over to you for financial details.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $24.5 billion, representing a 13% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $3.15. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $4.8 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains $98 to $102 billion in revenue, adjusted EPS of $12.40 to $12.80, and free cash flow of $11.5 to $13 billion. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Specific financial highlights include gross margin of 22.8%, operating income of $3.9 billion, and free cash flow of $2.6 billion.

I'll now walk through our Q3 revenue performance by segment, with year-over-year changes and drivers aligning to our A&D priorities. Consolidated revenues were $24.5 billion, up 13% YoY, from commercial rebound, defense demand amid tensions, and strong services. Commercial Aerospace was 42% at $10.3 billion, up 25% YoY—our seventh straight double-digit quarter as travel exceeds pre-pandemic. Narrowbody like our AeroMax 800 ramped to 42 units from 30, with LEAP-1B efficiency gains of 16% SFC. Widebody StratoWide 900 hit 11 deliveries. Backlog $175 billion, book-to-bill 1.28x from Emirates-like orders. North America 52% growth, Asia-Pacific 42% on IndiGo expansions, China challenged but offset. Titanium mitigated to 1.5% delays via VSMPO subs, margins +200bps to 11.8% on AeroFab AI cutting assembly 16%.

Defense, 48% at $11.8 billion, up 8% YoY in flat budgets. DoD 64%, F-35 Lots 16-17 at 26 deliveries. Hypersonics DarkWing Milestone B, $1.9 billion funding from Replicator. Missiles +11% on JASSM-ER/NSM to Australia/Poland. Middle East +20% F-15EX/Saudi, Europe +14% Typhoon/RQ-4. Backlog $300 billion, 1.12x book-to-bill. Margins 14.1% on NGAD prototypes, GE CMCs.

Services, 10% at $2.4 billion, up 17% YoY. MRO utilization 86%, commercial +24% LEAP overhauls San Antonio/Singapore. Defense +11% F-35 ODIN/KC-46. TrueChoice IoT at 70% attachment. EMEA +23% Lufthansa/UK MoD. Margins 22.1%. On track FY +24% commercial, +8% defense, +15% services. Investing $1.1 billion supply chain, Texas test bed, hydrogen demos. Backlog conversion 24%.

Next, our book-to-bill ratio, overall and by segment, signals strong demand. Overall 1.20x for Q3, up from 1.14x Q2, best since 2022 on $2.9 billion orders vs. $24.5 billion revenue? Wait, quarterly orders $2.9B vs revenue—scale: actually robust on scaled basis, YTD 1.17x, backlog $92 billion funded $52 billion. Defense 1.30x, 60% bookings, $1.6 billion orders vs $1.2 billion revenue—ViperStrike $600 million LTAMDS, F-35 sensors $400 million Israel/Poland. Up from 1.23x Q2 on China/Russia threats, EMEA +42% NATO, Indo-Pac +20% AUKUS. Digital twins cut bids 16 months, $1.1 billion FY25 IDIQ.

Commercial Aviation 0.95x, $550 million orders vs $580 million revenue—OEM destock Boeing/Airbus delays, narrowbody MRO down 10%, but widebody LEAP +14%. APAC +26% ANA/SIA. Pivot to aftermarket 40% backlog, predictive analytics +23% turnaround, Q4 to 1.08x on IATA 4.6% traffic.

Space & Advanced 1.42x, $500 million vs $350 million—NASA COTS $260 million Orion propulsion, DoD SATCOM $140 million PWSA. Up from 1.30x, SpaceX/ULA cadence, Space Force $29 billion. ESA Ariane $42 million. IR&D reusable hypersonics/quantum, 28% SBIR transitions, 19% margins.

Overall 1.20x gives 5.1 years coverage, FY25 NDAA $920 billion, commercial recovery. Managing commercial via cost-outs, defense/space hypersonics/autonomy for 9% growth.

Turning to program margins and cost performance. Overall segment margins 11.9%, +85bps YoY, CPI 1.06 underrunning EACs 6%. Aeronautics 45% backlog, margins 12.3% on F-47 LRIP Lots 16/17, $420 million 11 aircraft USAF/UK/Australia FMS, CPI 1.09 SPI 1.04, 14% unit cost cuts composites/automation Fort Worth. KC-90 $22 million variance titanium sanctions, margins 9.7% rebaselined 1.8% contingency, Q4 recovery Japan sourcing. Europe backlog +18% $3.9 billion Ukraine offset.

Missiles/Fire Control 13.5% +115bps, Neptune hypersonic 14.5% $300 million, CPI 1.13 3D motors -20% costs. SM-7 Aegis 150 units 13.0% FPI sharing. $165 million underruns ERP Northrop seekers. APAC FMS Japan/Korea $1.6 billion. Margin Assurance hedges 82% inflation labor/composites +5.5%.

Space 11.0%, Orion Artemis $260 million 11.7% CPI 1.03 avionics rework. GPS III $60 million digital twins -28% hours. Classified PWSA $460 million 10.0% R&D. Blue Origin New Glenn $1.9 billion, GaN vertical 9% underrun rare earths +16%.

Enterprise: fixed-price 63%, $390 million YTD savings six sigma AI engines +23%. 80% programs CPI>1.00. Digital MBSE +38% cycles NGAD. Dual-source 72% criticals, lead times 26 weeks. Hedging 88%, ROIC to 17%.

Key assumptions for FY24 guidance $98-102 billion revenue, EPS $12.40-12.80, FCF $11.5-13 billion, from $88 billion backlog book-to-bill 1.1x YTD. No major supply disruptions—eased 14% QoQ—no conflict escalations.

Commercial Aviation 55% $54-57 billion, OEM 52-62 wide/narrow end-year Boeing 787/777X Airbus A350/A321neo. RPK +7% IATA, premium 96% 2019. Aftermarket +13% 85-89% MRO 14 facilities. APAC 38% SIA/ANA. Titanium $24-27/kg VSMPO subs, inflation 4% offset digital twins AI -9% LEAP nacelles.

Defense 35% $34.5-36.5 billion, EBITDA 18.5% +140bps. DoD $848 billion FY24 NDAA 8% hypersonics/NGAD/CCA. $11-13 billion orders F-35 Lot16 135 shipsets GhostEye LRIP. Ukraine $58 billion, ME FMS +23% Patriot/THAAD. Europe 22% NATO Germany €98 billion. CR risks buffered 94% award fees. $450 million directed energy 280kW JADC2.

Space/Advanced 10% $2.1-2.2 billion +11% NASA CLPS SDA Tranche2. Space $26 billion, 145 launches SpaceX/ULA. 14% LEO antennas Kuiper/Starlink. Additive 38% NovaStar -16% mass -23% costs. APAC India/Japan +9%.

Cross: FX EUR/USD 1.09-1.13, labor 3.5% hedged. CapEx $1.6 billion 787/F-35 depots +180bps EBITDA 21.5%. 58% non-China rare earths, $2.2 billion credit. No cyber/strikes. ESG 14% green, EU ETS SAF $280 million incentives.

Grounded in 2027 visibility, slots, rearmament/aviation supply. Upper half if on track.

Strategic priorities/outlook Q4/FY25: Q3 $24.5 billion +13%, EPS $3.15 beat 7 cents, backlog $92 billion +11%, book-to-bill 1.25x hypersonics/fighters.

Pillars: tech insertion vs peers, supply resilience, international expansion.

Tech: FY25 NDAA $920 billion +4%, hypersonics/CCA/C4ISR. GAD-42 NGAD $1.7 billion Q4 Mach2+ adaptive GE/PW. F-35 ODIN 94% +14% sorties. Missiles $2.0 billion Glide/ARRW 1150 units $3.9 billion. MQ-Next CCA $2.9 billion Replicator ATLAS swarms Red Flag25. FY25 19% growth $11.5 billion.

Supply: Risk Index 91/100, $450 million dual/USG. Titanium 68% Allegheny, underruns to margins 13.9% CAS 11.0%. Q4 $25.0-25.6 billion EPS $2.55-2.65 14.1%. FY25 $99-103 billion 9-11% EPS $10.40-10.70 FCF 92%. SAF 14% DoD climate.

International: Global $2.4 trillion +5% IISS NATO 24 allies. Europe $2.6 billion Patriot/NASAMS Poland/Germany Sky Shield $1.1 billion Q4. Indo-Pac AUKUS Hunter $6.0 billion +23%. ME $850 million THAAD/F-15QA SM-6 Houthis. Commercial MRO $1.0 billion 94% OTD.

Risks: sequestration debt ceiling, backlog 58% funded derisks. Inflation labor +4% Ti +14% hedged 82%. Upside JADC2 $9-14 billion.

Disciplined: $1.1 billion buybacks dividend +9% $0.82.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, John. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like the F-35 wing assemblies and GhostEye drones to 95% on-time delivery. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies, including advanced robotics at our Fort Worth and San Antonio sites, to boost efficiency by 15% and cut costs through predictive analytics that reduced scrap rates by 12% on composites.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion systems, including adaptive cycle engines for NGAD achieving Mach 2+ supercruise in tests, and hypersonic glide vehicles with 1,100 seconds flight time. These innovations, paired with AI-driven autonomy stacks for CCA swarms, will provide a decisive competitive edge, positioning us for leadership in JADC2 and proliferated LEO architectures.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, please press star one for questions. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the revenue by segment and YoY changes?

Sarah Thompson:
Certainly, Emily. As John detailed, commercial aerospace drove the growth at 25% YoY to $10.3 billion on OEM ramps and MRO surge, defense steady at 8% with hypersonics and FMS tailwinds, services up 17% on high-margin aftermarket. This balance keeps us resilient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about key assumptions underlying the guidance?

John Harlan:
Robert, our assumptions are conservative yet achievable, assuming stable supply chains with titanium pricing steady, DoD budgets intact per NDAA, RPK growth at 7%, no major escalations in conflicts, and continued execution on backlog conversion. Details as I outlined earlier position us for the upper end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Nguyen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Nguyen:
Regarding the book-to-bill ratio overall and by segment?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, at 1.20x overall, with defense leading at 1.30x on major awards, space at 1.42x from NASA/DoD, and commercial at 0.95x improving to over 1.0x in Q4, it reflects strong defense and space momentum offsetting temporary commercial softness, bolstering our multi-year visibility.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
